content.text:
The Child Who Vanishes in a Blink

In crowded places like a store or an amusement park, the moment something catches your child's eye, they let go of your hand and dash off in an instant. When your child slips out of sight in that split second, a parent's heart drops.

Children let go out of curiosity. The real problem is that they don't know what to do when they get lost. That's why, just as much as preventing it, it matters to teach them ahead of time how to cope if they do get lost.

Curious about the story of lost-child prevention? Take a look at its lesson through pictures. Meet the key scenes of the tale too. Read it together with your child and talk about it. We've gathered many stories about when a child gets lost, child safety education, safety habit storybooks and more, all around 18. Hold Tight! Stay by Mom!

content.alt: 18. Hold Tight! Stay by Mom! - Why Knowing What to Do When Lost Matters
content.text:
Why Knowing What to Do When Lost Matters

If a child panics and runs around the moment they get lost, they become even harder to find. On the other hand, if they stop where they are and ask a safe adult for help, they can be reunited far more quickly and safely.

What matters is not scaring them with frightening stories, but teaching them specific actions they can take on their own in an urgent moment. A child who knows what to do stays calm even in a scary situation.
content.caption: Stop and ask for help, and you can be reunited.

content.alt: 18. Hold Tight! Stay by Mom! - Hori's Hold Tight, Stay by Mom Story
content.text:
Hori's Hold Tight, Stay by Mom Story

In "Hold Tight! Stay by Mom!", Hori also gets swept up by the balloon corner, lets go, and runs off. When he turns around, Mom and the cart are nowhere to be seen, and his eyes brim with tears.

Then he remembers Mom's words: 'If you get lost, stop right where you are!' Instead of running, Hori stops and takes a big breath. He walks up to a staff member wearing a green apron and says clearly, 'I lost my mom. My mom is Mother Tiger.' An announcement plays over the speakers, Mom comes running, and Hori nestles snugly into her arms.
content.caption: He clearly told the staff member his mom's name.

content.alt: 18. Hold Tight! Stay by Mom! - Let's Practice Together at Home
content.text:
Let's Practice Together at Home

After reading the book, set your own family safety promise. First, before going out, talk in advance about 'what will you do if we let go of hands?' and promise to wait in place.

Second, teach them that if they get lost, they should not wander around but stop and tell a staff member or a safe adult their parent's name. Third, rather than scaring them, reassure them that 'if you stop and ask for help, we will always find each other again.' Practicing saying their own name and their parent's name also helps.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions

Q. How do I start teaching lost-child prevention?

A. Turn the promise to hold hands tight and stay by Mom outside into a game. Repeating it often helps your child stay close on their own.

Q. How do I prepare for when my child gets lost?

A. Without scaring them, tell them ahead of time that if you get separated for a moment, they should stand right there and look for an adult who can help. Lost-child prevention is best taught not with fear but as a reassuring promise.

Q. Should they learn their own name and contact information?

A. If your child is old enough to speak, practicing their name and a parent's contact number like a game helps. Praising them when they remember it well builds their confidence.
